title: Per-locale rerank upgrade playbook and regression harness
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable, low-risk process for selecting, validating, and rolling out cross-encoder reranker upgrades across locales. The focus is quality (per-locale relevance), latency (tail P95/P99 and deploy-time budget), and scaling (inference throughput and cost). This ticket scopes the playbook, builds an automated regression harness that runs per-locale tests in CI, and defines canary rollout gates tied to Console dashboards.

Why now: We have multiple candidate cross-encoder variants and compact quantized builds. Past rollouts showed uneven regressions in non-en locales (see ENG-21034 and ENG-24678). We need an operationalized path to upgrade without regressions and with clear rollback criteria.

Success criteria:
- Automated per-locale evaluation suite integrated into CI that runs on PR and nightly jobs.
- Regression detection: drop in per-locale nDCG@10 or MRR > 2% triggers a failure/gating flag.
- Latency SLO gating: P95 increase > 10% or P99 increase > 20% blocks rollout.
- Canary rollout plan documented and wired to Console for automated metrics check and rollback.
- A small set of validated fallback models (quantized or smaller variants) available for immediate use if upgrade fails.
acceptance_criteria: Per-locale test harness (EN, ES, FR, DE, PT, JA, KO, ZH) added to rerank-eval CI pipeline
Evaluation reports stored in S3 and linked from Console with per-locale deltas
CI job fails for model PRs when any locale shows >2% quality regression or latency SLO breach
Canary rollout automation configured: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback if Console gates fail
Runbook added to Confluence with rollback steps, PR template, and required dashboard widgets
plan: Phase 1: Define per-locale datasets and metrics (gold queries + candidate pools). Acquire missing locales from partners and anonymized logs.
Phase 2: Implement evaluation harness: standardized TFRecords, evaluation runner, and threshold config. Add to GitHub Actions and nightly cluster job.
Phase 3: Integrate latency benchmarks using synthetic load harness tied to the runtime staging cluster and quantized builds.
Phase 4: Build canary rollout workflow in Console: gating rules, alerting, and automatic rollback playbook.
Phase 5: Run pilot upgrade for a low-traffic region (PT/ES) and collect metrics. Iterate thresholds and document lessons learned.
decisions: Use nDCG@10 and MRR as primary quality metrics (chosen for stability across list lengths).
Regression threshold set at 2% relative drop for quality and 10%/20% for P95/P99 latency respectively.
Initial locales for CI: EN, ES, FR, DE, PT, JA, KO, ZH (add others incrementally).
Quantized int8 variants will be evaluated first for latency gains; BF16/FP16 baselines retained for fallback comparisons.
risks: Dataset sparsity for low-traffic locales could produce noisy signals and false positives.
CI cost: nightly runs for many locales increases compute spend; need sampling strategy and caching of embeddings.
Model binary compatibility: new kernels or quantization paths may not have hot-path parity causing hidden regressions.
Automated rollback could oscillate if thresholds are too tight; requires smoothing and burn-in windows.
